question: What is the difference between a shallow copy and a deep copy of a Python list?
answer: A shallow copy of a Python list creates a new list with the same elements as the original list. [S1] This means that if you modify the elements of the original list, the changes will be reflected in the copy. [S1] However, if the elements are mutable objects (like other lists or dictionaries), the copy will share those objects with the original. [S1] This is in contrast to a deep copy, which creates a new list and recursively copies all elements, including mutable ones, into the new list [S1].

S2.title: Python Lecture Notes
S2.text: 4. Lists, Tuples, Sets and Dictionaries A list is an ordered, mutable sequence: nums = [3, 1, 2]. Common methods are append(x) to add at the end, insert(i, x), remove(x), pop() to remove and return the last item, and sort() to sort in place. The built-in sorted(nums) returns a new sorted list and leaves the original unchanged. List comprehensions build lists concisely: [n * n for n in nums if n > 1]. A tuple is an ordered but immutable sequence, written (1, 2). Tuples are used for fixed records and can be dictionary keys because they are hashable. A set stores unique, unordered elements and supports fast membership tests plus union (|), intersection (&) and difference (-). A dictionary maps keys to values: ages = {"Ali": 20, "Mona": 22}. S3.title: Python Debugging Playbook
S3.text:
3. Lookup Errors Compared
KeyError is raised when a dictionary key is missing. IndexError is raised when a sequence index is
out of range. AttributeError is raised when an object has no attribute of that name.
The message 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'append' almost always means a variable holds
None instead of a list. The classic cause is writing nums = nums.sort(), because list.sort() sorts in
place and returns None. Use nums.sort() on its own line or sorted(nums) when a new list is
needed.
dict.get(key, default) avoids a KeyError, while collections.defaultdict(list) creates a missing key with
an empty list the first time it is accessed, which makes grouping code shorter.

S4.title: Python Debugging Playbook
S4.text:
4. Performance Pitfalls
functools.lru_cache(maxsize=128) caches the results of a function for repeated arguments; the
default maxsize is 128 and maxsize=None removes the limit. Arguments must be hashable.
Building a long string with += inside a loop copies the string repeatedly; collect the pieces in a list
and call "".join(parts) once. A membership test with in is a linear scan for a list but an average
constant-time lookup for a set or dict, so convert a list to a set when you test membership many
times.
collections.Counter(words).most_common(3) returns the three most frequent items as (item, count)
pairs. Sorting with sorted(items, key=len) is faster and clearer than writing a comparison function.
